Expo 56 / React Native 0.85.3 navigation app using `expo-here-maps` for map + routing. Branch: `expo-experimental`.

**Why:** Building a UK checkpoints navigation mobile app for PeoplePerHour client.

**Stack:**
- `expo-here-maps` — HereMapsView, suggestPlaces, resolvePlace, showRoute, startGuidance/stopGuidance, clearRoute
- NativeWind v5 (Tailwind CSS classes in RN)
- @gorhom/bottom-sheet v5
- react-native-reanimated v4
- zustand v5
- expo-router (file-based routing)

**Architecture:**
- `src/app/index.tsx` — Main screen: HereMapsView fullscreen + Sheet (peek/expanded)
- `src/features/navigation/` — Route search feature:
  - `SheetSearch.tsx` — Full search UI (origin/destination + results + route summary)
  - `SheetSearchDecoy.tsx` — "Where to?" pill at peek state, expands sheet on press
  - `RoutePointField.tsx` — Individual input field (supports active text input or pressable display)
  - `RouteSummaryCard.tsx` — Duration/distance/ETA card + Start button
  - `SearchResultRow.tsx` — Search result item using Card component
  - `hooks/use-route-search.ts` — Main hook (origin, destination, active field, route flow)
  - `hooks/use-search.ts` — Debounced 250ms search via mapRef.suggestPlaces
  - `lib/format-route.ts` — formatDistance, formatDuration, formatEta helpers
  - `route-context.tsx` — RouteContext: isNavigating, etaSeconds, remainingMeters, maneuver
- `src/components/ui/sheet.tsx` — Sheet/SheetPeek/SheetExpanded/SheetReveal wrapping @gorhom
- `src/features/location/` — Location permission + useCurrentLocation hook

**expo-here-maps native module** (`modules/expo-here-maps/src/`, aliased as `expo-here-maps` in tsconfig):

Ref methods on `HereMapsViewRef`:
- Map: `setMapScheme(scheme)`, `enableFeatures(string[])`, `disableFeatures(string[])`, `setCameraPosition({lat,lng,animated?,bearing?,tilt?})`
- Search: `suggestPlaces(query, near: LatLng): GeoJsonFeatureCollection`, `resolvePlace(placeId): LatLng`
- Route (visual only): `showRoute(from, to, mode?): RouteSummary`, `clearRoute()`
- Multi-modal: `compareRoutes(from, to, modes[]): CompareRouteResult[]`
- Guidance: `startGuidance(from, to, mode?): RouteSummary`, `stopGuidance()`
- Location: `updateUserLocation(lat, lng, bearing?)`

View event props: `onMapError`, `onGuidanceProgress({remainingMeters,etaSeconds})`, `onManeuver({text})`, `onOffRoute({distanceFromRoute})`, `onArrived`, `onNavigableLocation({streetName?,speedLimit?})`

View props: `center?: MapCenter`, `bearing?: number`, `tilt?: number`

Constants:
- `MapSchemes`: NORMAL_DAY, NORMAL_NIGHT, SATELLITE, HYBRID_DAY, HYBRID_NIGHT, LITE_DAY, LITE_NIGHT, LITE_HYBRID_*, LOGISTICS_*, ROAD_NETWORK_*, TOPO_*
- `MapFeatures`: TRAFFIC_FLOW, TRAFFIC_INCIDENTS, TRAFFIC_LIGHTS, EXTRUDED_BUILDINGS, BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS, VEHICLE_RESTRICTIONS, SAFETY_CAMERAS, LANDMARKS, ENVIRONMENTAL_ZONES, CONGESTION_ZONES, LOW_SPEED_ZONES, TERRAIN, PUBLIC_TRANSIT, ROAD_EXIT_LABELS, SHADOWS, AMBIENT_OCCLUSION, CONTOURS, TRUCK_PREFERRED_ROADS
- `TransportModes`: car, truck, pedestrian, bicycle, scooter, taxi, bus

**Rule from AGENTS.md:** Always read https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v56.0.0/ before writing Expo code.

44	## Engineering Standard
45	
46	Write boring code only. Boring means: clear names, small files, small widgets, simple control flow, predictable state, obvious folder structure. No magic abstractions, no clever one-liners, no unnecessary packages, no framework cosplay, no sci-fi architecture names.

Don't add defensive handling for cases that can't happen. Don't introduce an abstraction for one call site. If an adjacent problem surfaces while fixing the asked-for one, name it in one line — don't fix it silently.
51	
52	## Product Standard
53	
54	The app must feel simple, fast, and human. Every change preserves or improves startup, responsiveness, scroll, readability, accessibility, localization readiness, and maintainability.
55	
56	No technical jargon in user-facing text.
57	
58	Bad → Good:
59	
60	```txt
61	Failed to mutate entity   → Could not save your changes. Please try again.
62	Auth token expired        → Your session expired. Please sign in again.
63	Invalid payload           → Please check the highlighted fields.

65	```
66	
67	## Performance Standard
68	
69	Assume this runs on low-end Android (Samsung J2-class). Target 60 FPS where reasonable.
70	
71	Optimize only where code clearly risks jank, rebuild waste, leaks, slow startup, or wasted work. Don't optimize blindly. The recurring offenders:
72	
73	- Heavy work, async calls, or expensive object creation inside `build()`.
74	- Rebuilding a whole screen for one small state change. Missing `const`.
75	- Large collections without `ListView.builder` / `GridView.builder` / slivers.

Use the state management already in the project — do not introduce Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, GetX, MobX, Redux, a custom event bus, or any new dependency unless the user approves it. Don't upgrade dependencies. Don't rewrite working architecture because you'd have done it differently.

# AGENTS.md

## Role

You are an autonomous senior Flutter cleanup engineer.

Inspect one requested folder or feature area, clean it up, verify it, open one focused PR. That's the whole job.

You are not redesigning the app, inventing architecture, adding features, or writing clever code. You are making the existing Flutter iOS/Android codebase cleaner, safer, faster, and easier for the next engineer (and real users) to understand.

## First Rule

Before anything, ask the user which folder or feature to work on. Do not inspect, edit, or plan until you have the target path.

That path is the only editable scope. Everything else is read-only context.

- You may import from outside the target folder.
- You may read outside it to learn project conventions.
- You may not edit outside it without explicit approval.

If a proper fix needs a change outside the folder, don't make it. List it under `Follow-up needed` in the PR.

## HERE SDK — local docs (I HAVE Navigation Tier so i have Licesense for it.)

You do not have HERE SDK / `here-sdk` knowledge in your head. Do not guess HERE API names, signatures, routing params, map options, or asset paths from memory.

A full local copy of the HERE SDK API reference, docs, and examples is set up in `here-sdk_local_doc/`. Use it as the source of truth. Find what you need with plain shell:

```sh
# locate the doc tree (don't assume the exact location)
find . -type d -name "here-sdk_local_doc"

# find an API, class, or method
grep -rn "HERE.routing.RoutingEngine" here-sdk_local_doc/
grep -rni "bottom sheet" here-sdk_local_doc/

# find an example or asset to reuse
grep -rln "MapMarker" here-sdk_local_doc/
find here-sdk_local_doc/ -name "*.png" -o -name "*.svg"
```

Read the local doc or example before calling any HERE API. If it isn't in `here-sdk_local_doc/`, say so — don't invent it.

## Engineering Standard

Write boring code only. Boring means: clear names, small files, small widgets, simple control flow, predictable state, obvious folder structure. No magic abstractions, no clever one-liners, no unnecessary packages, no framework cosplay, no sci-fi architecture names.

Clever code is technical debt with a short fuse. Readable code wins.

Change only what was asked. Don't refactor adjacent code you weren't pointed at. Don't add docstrings, type annotations, or comments to lines you didn't touch. Don't add defensive handling for cases that can't happen. Don't introduce an abstraction for one call site. If an adjacent problem surfaces while fixing the asked-for one, name it in one line — don't fix it silently.

## Product Standard

The app must feel simple, fast, and human. Every change preserves or improves startup, responsiveness, scroll, readability, accessibility, localization readiness, and maintainability.

No technical jargon in user-facing text.

Bad → Good:

```txt
Failed to mutate entity   → Could not save your changes. Please try again.
Auth token expired        → Your session expired. Please sign in again.
Invalid payload           → Please check the highlighted fields.
Something went wrong       → Could not update your profile. Check your connection and try again.
```

## Performance Standard

Assume this runs on low-end Android (Samsung J2-class). Target 60 FPS where reasonable.

Optimize only where code clearly risks jank, rebuild waste, leaks, slow startup, or wasted work. Don't optimize blindly. The recurring offenders:

- Heavy work, async calls, or expensive object creation inside `build()`.
- Rebuilding a whole screen for one small state change. Missing `const`.
- Large collections without `ListView.builder` / `GridView.builder` / slivers.
- Undisposed controllers, focus nodes, streams, animation controllers, listeners, timers, subscriptions.
- Un-debounced expensive input handlers.
- Unsized/uncached large images; gratuitous opacity, blur, shadow, shader, clipping, or animation.
- Blocking the first frame with avoidable work.

## Flutter & State Standards

Follow the project's existing conventions. Prefer official Flutter/Dart patterns over custom abstractions. Use the state management already in the project — do not introduce Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, GetX, MobX, Redux, a custom event bus, or any new dependency unless the user approves it. Don't upgrade dependencies. Don't rewrite working architecture because you'd have done it differently.

State must be explicit, inspectable, and safe across async and after disposal. Guard async UI updates:

```dart
if (!context.mounted) return;
```

## Folder Structure

Keep it boring and predictable. Follow whatever the project already uses — feature-first if that's the pattern, simple flat structure if that's the pattern. Consistency beats theory.

Feature-first reference (use only the layers that exist or are genuinely needed):

```txt
feature_name/
  data/        models/ repositories/ sources/
  domain/      entities/ use_cases/
  presentation/screens/ widgets/ controllers/
  l10n/
  feature_name.dart
```

Simple reference:

```txt
profile/
  profile_screen.dart
  profile_controller.dart
  profile_repository.dart
  widgets/ profile_header.dart profile_form.dart
```

Don't create empty folders, fake architecture, gratuitous file splits, or barrels the project doesn't already use.

## Naming

Clear, boring, searchable. Names explain purpose, not implementation trivia.

Good: `userProfile`, `saveButton`, `isSubmitting`, `loadOrders`, `paymentRepository`, `ProfileHeader`
Bad: `data`, `tmp`, `res`, `managerThing`, `handlerX`, `UltraProfileEngine`, `SmartFormOrchestrator`

- Widget file name matches the main exported widget.
- Class names describe their actual role; boolean names read like true/false statements; async method names describe the action.
- Avoid abbreviations unless standard in the project. Avoid `Helper`/`Manager`/`Service`/`Utils` unless the project already uses them consistently.
- No collisions with model fields, API fields, or DB columns. Magic numbers get named constants.

## Widgets

A screen file mostly composes smaller widgets. A widget has one job.

Avoid: 300-line screen files, business logic in `build()`, large nested ternaries, repeated padding/layout/loading/error/empty markup, anonymous widgets that should be extracted, stateful widgets where stateless suffices.

Prefer: extracted private widgets for local-only UI, reusable public widgets only when actually reused, and clear loading / success / failure / empty / disabled states on every interactive flow.

## Localization

All user-facing strings must be localizable — labels, titles, placeholders, helper text, validation messages, snack bars, dialogs, bottom sheets, errors, empty states, tooltips, accessibility labels. No hardcoded user-visible text in widgets.

Use the project's existing system (`AppLocalizations.of(context)`, `context.l10n`, `S.of(context)`, whatever it is). Don't invent a new one.

If Arabic is required but unavailable, use a placeholder — never invent translations:

```txt
[ar] English text here
```

## Error Handling

Never swallow errors. No empty `catch`. Never show raw exception/server/DB/token/stack-trace text to users. Log developer context where the project has logging; show sanitized human messages. Errors carry enough context to debug at 3 AM.

```dart
catch (error, stackTrace) {
  logger.error('Failed to load profile', error: error, stackTrace: stackTrace);
  state = const ProfileState.error(ProfileError.loadFailed);
}
```

Match the project's logging and state patterns.

## Validation

Validate user input before submission — required fields, and email/phone/numeric/date/selection where applicable. Don't trust client input. Show all relevant field errors at once. Keep messages localizable and validation logic out of large widget trees. Reuse existing validators. No new validation package without approval.

## Security

Don't weaken security.

- No secrets in the client. No logging tokens, passwords, OTPs, private IDs, or sensitive data.
- Don't pass sensitive tokens through routes unless that's already project convention.
- Validate route params, deep links, and external URLs before launching.
- Check permissions before showing or running privileged actions.
- Don't bypass or modify auth flows beyond safe null checks without approval.

## Data Flow

UI renders data; business logic lives outside widgets. Follow the project's equivalent of:

```txt
screen → controller/state → repository → data source
```

Screens don't hold complex API logic. Widgets receive data via parameters. Repositories hide data-source details. Models parse safely. Don't mix navigation, API calls, formatting, and validation in one widget. No duplicate fetch logic across screens.

## Navigation

Use the router pattern the project already uses — don't introduce a new one. Validate route arguments and deep-link inputs. Don't pass large objects or sensitive values through routes. Give a user-friendly fallback for missing/invalid route data.

## Platform & Accessibility

Targets iOS and Android. Avoid platform-specific behavior unless needed; when needed, isolate it, keep safe fallbacks, follow existing patterns, break neither platform. Handle denied and permanently-denied permissions clearly.

Accessibility basics: reasonably sized tap targets, semantic labels on icon-only buttons, labels or explicit decorative marking on meaningful images, readable text at large font sizes, never color alone to convey meaning, clearly identified invalid fields.

## Research

Trust official sources, not memory. Before using or changing an API, verify from primary sources: Flutter/Dart docs, package docs, changelogs, source code, Apple/Android platform docs — and for HERE, the local `here-sdk_local_doc/` tree. Avoid SEO tutorials, random blogs, outdated StackOverflow. Don't claim an API behaves a certain way unless verified or already proven in the codebase.

## Scope

Fix only: folder structure, naming consistency, localization gaps, error UX, validation/safe data handling, performance risks, widget readability, platform correctness, accessibility basics. Nothing else.

**Out of scope without approval:** new features/screens, visual redesigns, dependency upgrades or replacements, architecture/auth rewrites, backend/DB/API-contract changes, analytics, payment logic, release signing, CI/CD, generated files, native iOS/Android project files (unless the requested folder *is* native code), test rewrites (unless your scoped change breaks an existing test).

Notice something important but out of scope? List it under `Out of scope but noticed`.

## Workflow

Do every step in order. Don't skip.

**1. Ask for target.** Exact wording: `Which folder or feature should I clean up?` Wait for the answer.

**2. Inventory.** List every file under the target. Tag which scope categories apply to each. Mark files to leave untouched and outside files needed as read-only context. No edits before the inventory is done.

**3. Read context.** Learn the project's localization, routing, state, error-handling, logging, repository/data-source, model-parsing, folder-naming, and loading/error/empty patterns. Read 2–3 files that already do it right and match them. Don't invent your own.

**4. Plan.** A focused checklist grouped by category (Localization / Error UX / Validation / Performance / Widget cleanup / Naming / Folder structure / Accessibility). Only real, applicable items. No broad refactors.

**5. Fix in dependency order.** localization → models/validators → repositories/sources → controllers/state → screens → widgets → navigation glue → platform code (only if needed). After each edit, mentally check imports, null safety, names, l10n keys, rebuild behavior, disposal, and that it compiles.

**6. Performance review.** Re-scan changed UI for the offenders in the Performance Standard. Fix only clear in-scope issues.

**7. Verify.** Detect the project's commands. At minimum run `flutter analyze`. Run `flutter test` if tests exist and it's practical, and the lightest useful build if practical. Fix every error your changes caused. Don't disable lints to pass. Pre-existing unrelated warnings may remain.

**8. One PR.** One branch: `cleanup/<folder-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>` (e.g. `cleanup/profile-2026-05-01`). Clear, imperative, scope-prefixed commits:

```txt
fix(profile): localize profile form errors
fix(profile): reduce unnecessary profile screen rebuilds
fix(profile): validate profile route arguments
```

Group related changes when independently revertable. No vague messages, no giant unrelated commits.

## PR Description

Use this exact shape. If a section has no changes, write `- No changes.` Don't remove sections.

```md
## Summary
-

## Target folder
`path/to/folder`

## What changed
### Localization
-
### Error UX
-
### Validation and safety
-
### Performance
-
### Widget cleanup
-
### Naming and structure
-
### Accessibility
-

## Verification
- [ ] `flutter analyze`
- [ ] `flutter test`
- [ ] Debug build checked
- [ ] Checked on small screen size
- [ ] Checked on large screen size

## Follow-up needed
-

## Out of scope but noticed
-
```

## Communication

One good engineer to another. Direct, specific, honest. Open with substance, close when done.

Don't write: "Great work on this codebase." / "I've made some improvements." / "Hope this helps." / "This PR enhances the overall experience."

Do write: "This folder had three concrete problems: hardcoded copy, unclear loading states, and a screen that rebuilt too much during form input. The PR fixes those without changing the visual design or public APIs."

## Hard Stops

Stop and ask for approval before: editing outside the target folder; changing a public API contract; changing backend/auth/DB-schema behavior; adding or upgrading dependencies; touching generated files or native iOS/Android project config; redesigning UI; introducing a new architecture or state pattern; anything destructive.

## Final Rule

Small, verified, boring improvements only. A clean PR beats a heroic rewrite. The best code here is what another engineer understands in 30 seconds and safely changes in 6 months.

Base directory for this skill: /home/zaid/.claude/skills/grain-design-system

# Grain Design System — beta

A taste engine, not a theme catalog. Built from Linear, Vercel, Stripe, Raycast, Apple
HIG iOS 26, Material 3 Expressive, Refactoring UI, Rauno Freiberg's interaction work,
Emil Kowalski's animation rules, and the named anti-AI-slop critiques of 2024–2026.

Strong defaults with documented escape hatches. The skill enforces opinions; the
industry packs override them.

---

## HOW TO USE THIS SKILL

When a user asks for any UI:

1. **Calibrate taste first.** Before writing code, infer or ask:
   - **Category** — SaaS app / corporate marketing / engineering or B2B / mobile native
   - **Tone** — serious-precise / playful / editorial / brutalist
   - **Density** — Linear-dense / Apple-quiet / data-tabular
   - **Industry pack** — defaults to SaaS if unspecified
2. **Load the industry pack.** Read the matching file from `references/`:
   - `industry-saas.md` for SaaS / app interfaces
   - `industry-corporate.md` for marketing sites
   - `industry-engineering.md` for B2B, data-dense, industrial
   - `industry-mobile-ios.md` for iOS native + Flutter Cupertino
   - `industry-mobile-android.md` for Android native + Flutter Material
3. **Run the 25 anti-slop rules** in `references/anti-slop-rules.md`. These are checked
   on output, not just on intent.
4. **Pull tokens from foundation.** `references/foundation.md` has the OKLCH palette,
   spacing scale, radius scale, motion curves, and the Tailwind v4 `@theme` block.
5. **Cross-check components.** `references/components.md` has spec for every primitive
   with hard limits and escape hatches.
6. **Self-review before shipping.** Walk the output against the anti-slop checklist
   and report any rule violations with the override reason.

If you skip step 1, the output regresses to median AI slop. The calibration is the
single biggest lever in the entire system.

---

## REFERENCE FILES

Read these on demand, not all at once. Each is the authoritative source for its domain.

| File | When to load |
|---|---|
| `references/anti-slop-rules.md` | **Always** load before generating any UI |
| `references/foundation.md` | **Always** load — color, type, spacing, radius, motion tokens |
| `references/components.md` | Whenever generating buttons, forms, cards, tables, modals, lists, badges |
| `references/typography.md` | Picking typefaces, optical sizing, font pairings |
| `references/motion.md` | Any animation, transition, or interactive feedback |
| `references/accessibility.md` | WCAG 2.2 AA — every component must pass |
| `references/seo-clean-code.md` | Marketing sites, semantic HTML, Core Web Vitals |
| `references/tailwind-v4.md` | Setting up `@theme`, OKLCH tokens, container queries |
| `references/shadcn.md` | Customizing shadcn/ui without producing default-neutral slop |
| `references/industry-saas.md` | SaaS pack — Linear/Vercel/Stripe/Raycast grammar |
| `references/industry-corporate.md` | Corporate / marketing pack — Apple/Stripe/Anthropic |
| `references/industry-engineering.md` | B2B / data-dense / industrial pack |
| `references/industry-mobile-ios.md` | iOS 26 Liquid Glass mobile pack |
| `references/industry-mobile-android.md` | Material 3 Expressive mobile pack |

---

## THE FIVE LAWS

These override everything. If a request conflicts with a Law, push back before complying.

### Law 1 — Calibrate the personality before writing code.
SaaS app and marketing site live by different rules. Engineering tool and consumer
mobile app live by different rules. Without a personality decision, every interface
regresses to the same `bg-indigo-500` + Inter + `rounded-2xl` median. Make the
personality decision explicit at the top of every component or screen file (a comment
is fine).

### Law 2 — One accent color, semantic everything else.
The brand has exactly one accent. Status colors (success / warning / error / info) are
semantic, never branded. Neutral fills 90% of the surface. Three-or-more-color brand
palettes are banned in the default pack — only marketing hero gradients (Stripe-style
mesh) allow multi-hue, and only inside a clearly bounded section.

### Law 3 — Hierarchy comes from color and weight before size.
Body text is one size. Display heads are one size larger. Secondary text is the same
size as body but with reduced opacity or a muted token. Stop scaling text up and down
to communicate importance. Pull the reader's eye with weight (400 → 500 → 600) and
contrast (foreground → muted → subtle), not with 12px ↔ 18px noise.

### Law 4 — Motion only when it changes meaning.
Animate state changes, modal entries, list reorders, optimistic confirmations. Do not
animate keyboard-initiated actions, frequently-used dropdowns, or anything triggered
more than 50× per session. Frequency kills delight; reach for instant. Emil Kowalski's
rule: Raycast has no open animation because the user opens it hundreds of times a day.

### Law 5 — Density is a feature, not a bug.
2026's reference brands all moved toward higher density (Linear's calmer interface,
Stripe Sigma's tables, Datadog dashboards). Whitespace is a tool, not a default. For
app interfaces, prefer table rows 40–48px tall, list items at native platform minimums,
and information per screen over "breathing room." Marketing sites are the only place
generous whitespace is the default.

---

## THE 25 ANTI-SLOP RULES (SUMMARY)

The full rules with rationale and primary sources live in `references/anti-slop-rules.md`.
This is the shortlist for quick reference:

1. No `bg-indigo-500`, no `from-indigo-500 to-purple-600` gradients, no Tailwind default purple.
2. No center-stacked "H1 + subtitle + 2 CTAs" hero.
3. Inter is fine, but Inter + default Tailwind + default shadcn = instant slop. Differentiate.
4. No `rounded-2xl` or `rounded-3xl` on every surface. Pick a radius system per industry pack.
5. No three-column "icon + heading + paragraph" features grid as a default layout.
6. Card-everything syndrome is banned. Tables, lists, prose blocks exist.
7. The stock dashboard layout (sidebar + topbar + 4 stat cards + table) needs differentiation.
8. No ✨ sparkle emoji. No AI iconography. Don't telegraph the tool.
9. No glassmorphism on every surface. Glass is contextual (iOS Liquid Glass, specific overlays).
10. No 3D abstract humans, no floating geometric shapes, no unDraw / Storyset.
11. No generic CTA pair ("Get started for free" + "Watch demo"). Single CTA per section.
12. No "Trusted by" grayscale logo wall as a default.
13. The shadcn default neutral theme is banned. Override `--primary`, `--radius`, font.
14. No lorem-ipsum-feeling copy. Concrete copy referencing the real user and outcome.
15. No drop shadows on everything. Use background contrast for elevation.
16. No pure `#000` text on `#fff`. Use desaturated near-black (`oklch(20% 0.04 265)`).
17. No default Material/Bootstrap blue links. Match brand or use a neutral underline.
18. No full-viewport hero gradient backgrounds as default.
19. No identical card hover (`scale(1.05) + shadow-2xl`). Translate-Y + border shift.
20. No loading spinner that causes layout shift. Fixed-width buttons swap label for spinner.
21. No modal-centered-with-blur on mobile. Use bottom sheet (Vaul).
22. No flat-illustration empty states with "No data yet" headline. Explain what the screen becomes.
23. No auto-animate on enter for everything. Animate only what changes meaning.
24. Body text below 15px is banned. 16px desktop minimum, 17px mobile.
25. No body fonts at weight 300 — illegible at small sizes.

## DEFAULT TAILWIND v4 + shadcn STACK

Recommended starting point for any web project:

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 App Router (or Vite + React 19 if no SSR needed)
- **Styling**: Tailwind v4 with `@theme` (CSS-first, no JS config)
- **Components**: shadcn/ui as primitives, customized per `references/shadcn.md`
- **Icons**: Phosphor Icons (consistent weight, broader than Lucide). Lucide acceptable
  for app chrome only.
- **Motion**: CSS animations + transitions for predetermined motion; Framer Motion
  ONLY for interruptible / gesture-driven motion.
- **Toasts**: Sonner (by Emil Kowalski).
- **Mobile sheets**: Vaul (by Emil Kowalski).
- **Command palette**: cmdk (by Paco Coursey / Rauno Freiberg).
- **Fonts**: Geist (free, OFL) as default. Override per industry pack.
- **Data viz**: Recharts for general charts, Tremor for KPI dashboards, visx for custom.

---

## ESCAPE HATCH SYNTAX

When generating code, document deviations from defaults using inline comments:

```tsx
// GRAIN OVERRIDE: industry=engineering — using 6px radius for B2B feel
<Card className="rounded-md">

// GRAIN OVERRIDE: marketing — Stripe-style gradient mesh hero
<section className="bg-gradient-to-br from-[oklch(95%_0.08_30)] via-[oklch(92%_0.1_280)] to-[oklch(94%_0.06_350)]">

// GRAIN OVERRIDE: anti-slop rule #2 — single CTA per hero (intentional break of "two CTAs")
```

Every deviation needs a reason. "It looks better" is not a reason; "industry pack
requires it" or "user explicitly asked" or "anti-slop rule conflicts with a stronger
rule" are reasons.

---

## SELF-REVIEW CHECKLIST

Before finishing a UI generation, walk this checklist out loud (or in a comment):

- [ ] **Personality**: declared category, tone, density, industry pack
- [ ] **Color**: one accent, semantic neutrals, no Tailwind default purple/indigo
- [ ] **Type**: not Inter-default; not weight 300 body; display has negative tracking
- [ ] **Radius**: systematic, not `rounded-2xl` on everything
- [ ] **Shadows**: only on elevated surfaces (modals, dropdowns), not on every card
- [ ] **Hierarchy**: weight + color drive importance, not just size
- [ ] **States**: every interactive has default / hover / focus-visible / active / disabled / loading
- [ ] **A11y**: focus rings 2px + 3:1 contrast; tap targets ≥44pt mobile / ≥24px web minimum
- [ ] **Motion**: only state-meaningful animations; reduced-motion fallback
- [ ] **SEO**: semantic HTML, one H1, meta tags, OG image (marketing only)
- [ ] **Anti-slop**: ran the 25 rules; flagged any intentional breaks with reason

If three or more items fail, regenerate the component, don't patch it.

71	## The Material 3 Color System
72	
73	M3 introduces **roles** instead of named colors. Each role has an `on*` companion
74	(for text/icon on that surface) and `*-container` variants (for backgrounds that
75	sit on top of the base).
76	
77	### Primary palette
78	
79	```
80	primary               — primary brand surface color (e.g., FAB background)
81	onPrimary             — text/icon on primary
82	primaryContainer      — softer container holding primary content
83	onPrimaryContainer    — text on primary container
84	```
85	
86	Same pattern for `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `inverseSurface`.
87	
88	### Full M3 Color Roles
89	
90	```
91	primary, onPrimary, primaryContainer, onPrimaryContainer
92	secondary, onSecondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer
93	tertiary, onTertiary, tertiaryContainer, onTertiaryContainer
94	error, onError, errorContainer, onErrorContainer
95	background, onBackground
96	surface, onSurface
97	surfaceVariant, onSurfaceVariant
98	surfaceDim, surfaceBright
99	surfaceContainerLowest, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer,
100	  surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest
101	inverseSurface, inverseOnSurface, inversePrimary
102	outline, outlineVariant
103	scrim, shadow
104	```
105	
106	13-tone palettes generate these from a single source color. With **Material You**,
107	that source color comes from the user's wallpaper at runtime.
108	
109	### 3:1 contrast minimum for roles
110	
111	All `on*` colors guarantee 3:1 contrast against their base. For body text use
112	`onSurface` on `surface` (always passes 4.5:1).

116	```kotlin

118	  colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme(),

122	    Text("Hello", color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface)
123	  }
124	}
125	```

131	    if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
132	    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
133	  }
134	  isSystemInDarkTheme() -> darkColorScheme()
135	  else -> lightColorScheme()
136	}

366	ModalBottomSheet(
367	  onDismissRequest = { coroutineScope.launch { sheetState.hide() } },
368	  sheetState = sheetState,
369	  dragHandle = { BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle() }
370	) {
371	  FilterContent()
372	}
373	```
374	
375	Rounded top corners (28dp). Drag handle visible by default. Swipe-down dismisses.
376	
377	---
378	
379	## FAB and FAB Menu (NEW in M3 Expressive)
380	
381	### Floating Action Button
382	
383	```kotlin
384	FloatingActionButton(onClick = { compose() }) {
385	  Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, contentDescription = "Compose")
386	}
387	
388	// Extended (with text)
389	ExtendedFloatingActionButton(
390	  onClick = { compose() },
391	  icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, null) },
392	  text = { Text("Compose") }
393	)
394	
395	// Small / Large variants
396	SmallFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
397	LargeFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
398	```
399	
400	### FAB Menu (NEW)
401	
402	When a single action isn't enough, FAB expands into a menu of secondary actions.
403	M3 Expressive introduces this as a stock component.
404	
405	```kotlin
406	FloatingActionButtonMenu(
407	  expanded = expanded,
408	  button = {
409	    ToggleFloatingActionButton(
410	      checked = expanded,
411	      onCheckedChange = { expanded = it }
412	    ) {
413	      Icon(Icons.Default.Add, null)
414	    }
415	  }
416	) {
417	  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Email, null) }, text = { Text("Email") })
418	  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Call, null) }, text = { Text("Call") })
419	  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Message, null) }, text = { Text("Message") })
420	}
421	```
422	
423	Replaces the older "speed dial" pattern.
424	
425	---
426	
427	## Toolbars — Docked and Floating (NEW)
428	
429	M3 Expressive deprecates the Bottom App Bar in favor of:
430	
431	### Docked Toolbar
432	
433	```kotlin
434	DockedToolbar(
435	  modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp),
436	  navigationIcon = { IconButton(...) { Icon(...) } },
437	  actions = {
438	    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, null) }
439	    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.MoreVert, null) }
440	  }
441	)
442	```
443	
444	### Floating Toolbar
445	
446	Translucent material, floats above content like iOS Liquid Glass equivalent.
447	
448	```kotlin
449	FloatingToolbar(
450	  modifier = Modifier
451	    .align(Alignment.BottomCenter)
452	    .padding(16.dp)
453	) {
454	  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatBold, null) }
455	  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatItalic, null) }
456	  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatUnderlined, null) }
457	}
458	```
459	
460	Use for: text editor formatting bars, contextual action sets, media player controls.
461	
462	---
463	
464	## Lists
465	
466	### List Item Spec (M3)
467	
468	| Lines | Height (no avatar) | Height (with avatar) |
469	|---|---|---|
470	| 1 line | 48dp | 56dp |
471	| 2 lines | 64dp | 72dp |
472	| 3 lines | 88dp | 88dp |
473	
474	Always 16dp horizontal padding.
475	
476	```kotlin
477	ListItem(
478	  headlineContent = { Text("Project Apollo") },
479	  supportingContent = { Text("Last updated 3 hours ago") },
480	  leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Folder, null) },
481	  trailingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.ChevronRight, null) },
482	  modifier = Modifier.clickable { open() }
483	)
484	```
485	
486	### Dividers
487	
488	Use `HorizontalDivider()` between sections, not between every item. Material 3
489	deprecated the always-divided list in favor of section-only dividers.
490	
491	---
492	
493	## Motion — Springs Replace Easing
494	
495	M3 Expressive replaces fixed-duration easing with **spring physics tokens** as the
496	default for important transitions.
497	
498	### Spring tokens
499	
500	```kotlin
501	// In Compose, the default for state animations
502	spring<Float>(
503	  dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy,
504	  stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMedium
505	)
506	
507	// Categories
508	Spring.DampingRatioHighBouncy
509	Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy
510	Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy
511	Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy
512	
513	Spring.StiffnessHigh
514	Spring.StiffnessMedium
515	Spring.StiffnessMediumLow
516	Spring.StiffnessLow
517	Spring.StiffnessVeryLow
518	```
519	
520	### Easing curves (still available for non-spring)
521	
522	```kotlin
523	MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier              // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
524	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier            // important transitions
525	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // incoming elements
526	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // outgoing
527	```
528	
529	### Duration tokens
530	
531	```
532	short1 = 50ms
533	short2 = 100ms
534	short3 = 150ms
535	short4 = 200ms
536	medium1 = 250ms
537	medium2 = 300ms
538	medium3 = 350ms
539	medium4 = 400ms
540	long1 = 450ms
541	long2 = 500ms
542	long3 = 550ms
543	long4 = 600ms
544	extraLong1 = 700ms
545	extraLong2 = 800ms
546	extraLong3 = 900ms
547	extraLong4 = 1000ms
548	```
549	
550	Default for UI feedback: `short3` (150ms) to `medium1` (250ms).
551	
552	### When to use spring vs easing
553	
554	- **Spring**: drag, gesture release, shape morphing, important state changes.
555	- **Easing**: enter/exit, predictable transitions, simple property changes.
556	
557	---
558	
559	## Shape System
560	
561	M3 has a shape system with five named tokens:
562	
563	```
564	extraSmall = 4dp
565	small = 8dp
566	medium = 12dp
567	large = 16dp
568	extraLarge = 28dp
569	full = 9999dp (pill)
570	```
571	
572	Applied per-component default:
573	- Buttons → full (pill)
574	- Cards → medium (12dp)
575	- Modals / sheets → extraLarge (28dp)
576	- Inputs → extraSmall (4dp)
577	- Snackbars → extraSmall
578	
579	In Compose:
580	```kotlin
581	Card(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium) { ... }
582	```
583	
584	---
585	
586	## Snackbars (the Toast equivalent)
587	
588	```kotlin
589	val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
590	val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
591	
592	Scaffold(
593	  snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
594	) { padding ->
595	  Button(onClick = {
596	    scope.launch {
597	      snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
598	        message = "Project saved",
599	        actionLabel = "Undo",
600	        duration = SnackbarDuration.Short
601	      )
602	    }
603	  }) { Text("Save") }
604	}
605	```
606	
607	- Position: bottom of screen.
608	- Duration: Short (~4s) / Long (~7s) / Indefinite.
609	- One snackbar at a time.
610	- Includes action when reversible.
611	
612	---
613	
614	## Material You Dynamic Color
615	
616	Android 12+ supports user-wallpaper-derived themes. Opt in:
617	
618	```kotlin
619	val colorScheme = when {
620	  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
621	    val context = LocalContext.current
622	    if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
623	    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
624	  }
625	  darkTheme -> darkColorScheme()
626	  else -> lightColorScheme()
627	}
628	```
629	
630	For apps where brand identity is critical, **don't** use dynamic color — provide a
631	fixed `ColorScheme`. For consumer apps where personalization is welcome (Calendar,
632	Notes, Messages), opt in.
633	
634	---
635	
636	## The 15 Android Mobile Rules
637	
638	**1.** **48dp minimum tap targets.** Material guideline, hard floor.
639	
640	**2.** **Use Material Components**, don't reinvent buttons, sliders, switches.
641	
642	**3.** **Roboto Flex** as the default typeface; weight contrast > size contrast.
643	
644	**4.** **Pill-shaped buttons** as default (M3 Expressive).
645	
646	**5.** **Bottom navigation 64dp**, max 5 items, labels always visible.
647	
648	**6.** **Large flexible top app bars** for top-level destinations; small for drill-down.
649	
650	**7.** **Modal bottom sheets** for actions/filters, not centered dialogs.
651	
652	**8.** **Spring physics** for state-meaningful motion, not fixed easing.
653	
654	**9.** **Shape morphing on button press** (M3 Expressive default).
655	
656	**10.** **Dynamic color** for consumer apps; fixed scheme for brand-critical apps.
657	
658	**11.** **FAB Menu** for multi-action primary; FAB for single primary.
659	
660	**12.** **Floating Toolbars** for contextual action sets (deprecated Bottom App Bar).
661	
662	**13.** **Material 3 list item heights** strict: 48 / 56 / 64 / 72 / 88dp.
663	
664	**14.** **TalkBack labels** on every Icon-only button (`contentDescription`).
665	
666	**15.** **Test with TalkBack on**, large font size (200%), and dark theme.
667	
668	---
669	
670	## Flutter Material (cross-platform Android target)
671	
672	```dart
673	MaterialApp(
674	  theme: ThemeData(
675	    useMaterial3: true,
676	    colorSchemeSeed: Color(0xFF5E6AD2),
677	    typography: Typography.material2021(),
678	  ),
679	  home: Scaffold(
680	    appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Home')),
681	    body: ListView(
682	      children: [
683	        ListTile(
684	          title: Text('Item'),
685	          trailing: Icon(Icons.chevron_right),
686	        ),
687	      ],
688	    ),
689	    floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
690	      onPressed: () { },
691	      child: Icon(Icons.add),
692	    ),
693	    bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
694	      destinations: [
695	        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.home), label: 'Home'),
696	        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.search), label: 'Search'),
697	      ],
698	      selectedIndex: 0,
699	      onDestinationSelected: (i) { },
700	    ),
701	  ),
702	)
703	```
704	
705	Flutter's M3 support as of 2026 includes most M3 Expressive components, with FAB
706	Menu and Floating Toolbar landing in 2025–2026 updates.
707	
708	---
709	
710	## Apple vs Material — The Contradictions Table
711	
712	Cross-platform apps must respect platform conventions. Here's where the systems
713	diverge:
714	
715	| Concern | iOS | Material 3 |
716	|---|---|---|
717	| Primary action position | Trailing (right) in nav | Bottom right (FAB) or right in app bar |
718	| Modal style | Bottom sheet with detents | Modal bottom sheet OR dialog |
719	| Back navigation | Top-left chevron + label | Top-left arrow icon |
720	| Top nav title | Large title that collapses | Small or Large Flexible app bar |
721	| Tap target | 44pt | 48dp |
722	| Font | SF Pro variable | Roboto Flex variable |
723	| Hierarchy driver | Size + weight (Dynamic Type) | Weight > size (Bold over Big) |
724	| Button shape default | Capsule (`.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`) | Pill |
725	| Motion default | Smooth ease | Spring physics |
726	| Tab bar height | ~49pt (now glass, minimize on scroll) | 64dp (down from 80dp) |
727	| Empty space treatment | Generous | Slightly tighter |
728	| Color generation | Custom or system blue | Material You from wallpaper |
729	
730	For cross-platform: provide a platform-aware shim layer. Don't ship Material UI to
731	iOS or Cupertino UI to Android.
732	
733	---
734	
735	## Hard Bans for Android Pack
736	
737	- ❌ iOS-style centered dialogs on Android (use bottom sheets).
738	- ❌ Tap targets below 48dp.
739	- ❌ Hardcoded colors that ignore Material You / dynamic theming.
740	- ❌ Bottom app bars (deprecated in M3 Expressive; use Docked/Floating Toolbar).
741	- ❌ Old M3 navigation bar heights (80dp) — use 64dp.
742	- ❌ Bold selected labels in nav bar (M3 Expressive changed this default).
743	- ❌ Fixed-duration easing for state-meaningful transitions (use springs).
744	- ❌ Pre-Roboto-Flex fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans) when Roboto Flex is available.
745	- ❌ Ignoring Dynamic Type / font scale settings.
746	- ❌ Snackbars stacking (one at a time, latest wins).
747	- ❌ FABs that don't expand to FAB Menu when multiple actions exist.
748	- ❌ Custom toggles / sliders when Material variants suffice.
749

# Industry Pack — Mobile Android (Material 3 Expressive)

For Android apps built with Jetpack Compose or XML views, and Flutter apps using
Material widgets. Anchored to **Material 3 Expressive**, announced at the
**Android Show I/O Edition** on **May 13, 2025**, with general availability in
2025–2026 across Android 16, Wear OS 6, and Material Components.

Reference points: Google's flagship apps (Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps,
Messages, Drive, YouTube), **Material You** showcases, **Linear Android**,
**Notion Android**, **Spotify**, **Twitter/X**, **TickTick, Todoist**, **Pocket
Casts, Plex, Tasker, Microsoft Outlook for Android**.

---

## Pack Identity

Material 3 Expressive emphasizes:

- **Spring-based motion** as the default (replacing fixed easing curves)
- **Shape morphing** — components change shape on press (pill → rounded square)
- **Larger, bolder typography** with weight variation as the primary hierarchy
  driver (Bold over Big)
- **Color expressiveness** via dynamic Material You palette generation
- **Floating Toolbars / FAB Menus** replacing bottom app bars
- **Pill-shaped buttons** as the new default
- **5 button sizes** (XS / S / M / L / XL)
- **48dp minimum tap target** (always)
- **Navigation bar now 64dp** (down from 80dp in Material 3 stock)

---

## Token Overrides

```css
:root[data-pack="android"] {
  /* M3 dynamic color — use the user's wallpaper-based primary by default */
  --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.16 280);          /* default purple, will be overridden by Material You */
  --color-accent-fg: oklch(99% 0.01 280);
  --color-accent-soft: oklch(95% 0.04 280);
  --color-accent-strong: oklch(50% 0.18 280);

  /* M3 radii */
  --radius-button: 9999px;                      /* pill */
  --radius-input: 0.25rem;                      /* 4dp */
  --radius-card: 0.75rem;                       /* 12dp */
  --radius-modal: 1.75rem;                      /* 28dp - M3 modal corner */
  --radius-bottomsheet: 1.75rem;                /* 28dp top corner only */

  /* Roboto Flex variable */
  --font-sans: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-display: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;

  /* M3 leading */
  --leading-display: 1.12;
  --leading-headline: 1.25;
  --leading-title: 1.4;
  --leading-body: 1.45;
  --leading-label: 1.3;
}
```

For pure Material You (wallpaper-driven):
```css
:root[data-pack="android-you"] {
  --color-accent: oklch(var(--m3-primary));     /* sourced from system at runtime */
}
```

---

## The Material 3 Color System

M3 introduces **roles** instead of named colors. Each role has an `on*` companion
(for text/icon on that surface) and `*-container` variants (for backgrounds that
sit on top of the base).

### Primary palette

```
primary               — primary brand surface color (e.g., FAB background)
onPrimary             — text/icon on primary
primaryContainer      — softer container holding primary content
onPrimaryContainer    — text on primary container
```

Same pattern for `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `inverseSurface`.

### Full M3 Color Roles

```
primary, onPrimary, primaryContainer, onPrimaryContainer
secondary, onSecondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer
tertiary, onTertiary, tertiaryContainer, onTertiaryContainer
error, onError, errorContainer, onErrorContainer
background, onBackground
surface, onSurface
surfaceVariant, onSurfaceVariant
surfaceDim, surfaceBright
surfaceContainerLowest, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer,
  surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest
inverseSurface, inverseOnSurface, inversePrimary
outline, outlineVariant
scrim, shadow
```

13-tone palettes generate these from a single source color. With **Material You**,
that source color comes from the user's wallpaper at runtime.

### 3:1 contrast minimum for roles

All `on*` colors guarantee 3:1 contrast against their base. For body text use
`onSurface` on `surface` (always passes 4.5:1).

### In Compose

```kotlin
MaterialTheme(
  colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme(),
  typography = Typography(),
) {
  Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface) {
    Text("Hello", color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface)
  }
}
```

For dynamic Material You:
```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  isSystemInDarkTheme() -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

---

## Typography — The 15-Token Scale

M3 has 15 typography tokens (5 roles × 3 sizes). Apply via `MaterialTheme.typography`.

| Token | Size | Weight | Line height | Letter spacing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Display Large** | 57sp | Regular 400 | 64sp | -0.25 |
| **Display Medium** | 45sp | Regular 400 | 52sp | 0 |
| **Display Small** | 36sp | Regular 400 | 44sp | 0 |
| **Headline Large** | 32sp | Regular 400 | 40sp | 0 |
| **Headline Medium** | 28sp | Regular 400 | 36sp | 0 |
| **Headline Small** | 24sp | Regular 400 | 32sp | 0 |
| **Title Large** | 22sp | Regular 400 | 28sp | 0 |
| **Title Medium** | 16sp | Medium 500 | 24sp | 0.15 |
| **Title Small** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
| **Body Large** | 16sp | Regular 400 | 24sp | 0.5 |
| **Body Medium** | 14sp | Regular 400 | 20sp | 0.25 |
| **Body Small** | 12sp | Regular 400 | 16sp | 0.4 |
| **Label Large** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
| **Label Medium** | 12sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |
| **Label Small** | 11sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |

In Compose:
```kotlin
Text("Title", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
Text("Body copy", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
Text("Button", style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge)
```

### Roboto Flex variable

M3 Expressive (2025) ships **Roboto Flex** as the primary typeface — variable axes:
- Weight: 100–1000
- Width: 25–151%
- Optical size: 8–144
- Slant, grade, ascender height, descender depth, counter width, all variable

The "Bold over Big" principle: use weight (500 → 700) to convey hierarchy on the
same scale, instead of jumping size tokens.

### Display Flexible Variants (M3 Expressive only)

New in 2025: "Display Medium Flexible" and "Display Large Flexible" let apps use
larger, more expressive typography for product moments. Used in Google's flagship
apps for empty states, onboarding, hero moments.

---

## Buttons — 5 Sizes, 5 Styles

M3 Expressive ships **5 button sizes** and **5 button styles**.

### Sizes

| Size | Height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **XS** | 32dp | Inline, dense lists, chips-adjacent |
| **S** | 36dp | Secondary actions in tight spaces |
| **M** | 40dp | Default |
| **L** | 48dp | Primary actions, mobile CTAs |
| **XL** | 56dp | Hero CTAs, "Continue" in onboarding |

```kotlin
Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Default M") }
Button(onClick = { }, modifier = Modifier.height(48.dp)) { Text("L") }
Button(
  onClick = { },
  modifier = Modifier.height(56.dp),
  contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 24.dp),
) { Text("XL") }
```

### Styles

| Style | Background | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Filled** | `primary` | Primary action per screen |
| **Filled Tonal** | `secondaryContainer` | Co-equal action, softer than filled |
| **Elevated** | `surface` + shadow | Action that needs to lift off background |
| **Outlined** | transparent + outline | Secondary action |
| **Text** | transparent | Lowest-emphasis action, links |

```kotlin
Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Filled") }              // primary
FilledTonalButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Tonal") }    // secondary
ElevatedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Elevated") }
OutlinedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Outlined") }
TextButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Text") }
```

### Pill shape default, shape-morphs on press

M3 Expressive defaults all buttons to pill shape. On press, the shape morphs to
a slightly more rounded square via spring animation. The default is enabled when
using `ButtonDefaults.shape`.

```kotlin
Button(
  onClick = { },
  shape = ButtonDefaults.shape       // pill, morphs on press
) { Text("Action") }
```

### Icon buttons

```kotlin
IconButton(onClick = { }) {
  Icon(Icons.Default.Settings, contentDescription = "Settings")
}

// Toggleable
IconToggleButton(checked = isChecked, onCheckedChange = { isChecked = it }) {
  Icon(
    if (isChecked) Icons.Filled.Favorite else Icons.Outlined.FavoriteBorder,
    contentDescription = "Like"
  )
}
```

48dp tap target minimum. Always provide `contentDescription` for TalkBack.

---

## Navigation Bar (Bottom Nav)

Material 3 Expressive: **64dp height** (reduced from M3 standard 80dp). Active
indicator: 56dp pill behind the selected icon.

```kotlin
NavigationBar(modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp)) {
  navItems.forEach { item ->
    NavigationBarItem(
      icon = { Icon(item.icon, contentDescription = item.label) },
      label = { Text(item.label) },
      selected = currentRoute == item.route,
      onClick = { navigate(item.route) }
    )
  }
}
```

### Behaviors

- Active label not bold by default (M3 Expressive change — was bold in original M3).
- Labels always visible (selected and unselected).
- 3–5 items max. >5 items: use Navigation Drawer or Navigation Rail.

### Material You Color

Selected item indicator uses `secondaryContainer`. Icons use `onSurfaceVariant`
(unselected) → `onSecondaryContainer` (selected).

---

## Top App Bars

Four variants:

| Variant | Height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Small** | 64dp | Default for nested screens |
| **Center-aligned Small** | 64dp | Title centered (Material You style) |
| **Medium Flexible** | ~112dp | Important pages with extra space |
| **Large Flexible** | ~152dp | Hero pages, top-level destinations |

```kotlin
// Small top app bar
TopAppBar(
  title = { Text("Inbox") },
  navigationIcon = {
    IconButton(onClick = { /* back */ }) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowBack, contentDescription = "Back")
    }
  },
  actions = {
    IconButton(onClick = { /* search */ }) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.Search, contentDescription = "Search")
    }
  }
)

// Large top app bar that collapses on scroll
LargeTopAppBar(
  title = { Text("Inbox", style = MaterialTheme.typography.displaySmall) },
  scrollBehavior = scrollBehavior
)
```

### Scroll behaviors

- `pinnedScrollBehavior` — stays at top
- `enterAlwaysScrollBehavior` — collapses on scroll down, reappears on scroll up
- `exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior` — collapses to small variant, large only at top

Large Flexible is the equivalent of iOS's "large title" — big at top, collapses
to small on scroll.

---

## Bottom Sheets

Two variants:

### Standard Bottom Sheet

Inline with content (e.g., Google Maps location details). Always visible at
collapsed state, expands on drag.

```kotlin
BottomSheetScaffold(
  sheetContent = { LocationDetails() },
  sheetPeekHeight = 128.dp,
) { padding ->
  MapView(padding)
}
```

### Modal Bottom Sheet

Overlay with scrim. Used for actions, filters, share sheets.

```kotlin
val sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState()
val coroutineScope = rememberCoroutineScope()

ModalBottomSheet(
  onDismissRequest = { coroutineScope.launch { sheetState.hide() } },
  sheetState = sheetState,
  dragHandle = { BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle() }
) {
  FilterContent()
}
```

Rounded top corners (28dp). Drag handle visible by default. Swipe-down dismisses.

---

## FAB and FAB Menu (NEW in M3 Expressive)

### Floating Action Button

```kotlin
FloatingActionButton(onClick = { compose() }) {
  Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, contentDescription = "Compose")
}

// Extended (with text)
ExtendedFloatingActionButton(
  onClick = { compose() },
  icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, null) },
  text = { Text("Compose") }
)

// Small / Large variants
SmallFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
LargeFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
```

### FAB Menu (NEW)

When a single action isn't enough, FAB expands into a menu of secondary actions.
M3 Expressive introduces this as a stock component.

```kotlin
FloatingActionButtonMenu(
  expanded = expanded,
  button = {
    ToggleFloatingActionButton(
      checked = expanded,
      onCheckedChange = { expanded = it }
    ) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.Add, null)
    }
  }
) {
  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Email, null) }, text = { Text("Email") })
  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Call, null) }, text = { Text("Call") })
  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Message, null) }, text = { Text("Message") })
}
```

Replaces the older "speed dial" pattern.

---

## Toolbars — Docked and Floating (NEW)

M3 Expressive deprecates the Bottom App Bar in favor of:

### Docked Toolbar

```kotlin
DockedToolbar(
  modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp),
  navigationIcon = { IconButton(...) { Icon(...) } },
  actions = {
    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, null) }
    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.MoreVert, null) }
  }
)
```

### Floating Toolbar

Translucent material, floats above content like iOS Liquid Glass equivalent.

```kotlin
FloatingToolbar(
  modifier = Modifier
    .align(Alignment.BottomCenter)
    .padding(16.dp)
) {
  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatBold, null) }
  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatItalic, null) }
  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatUnderlined, null) }
}
```

Use for: text editor formatting bars, contextual action sets, media player controls.

---

## Lists

### List Item Spec (M3)

| Lines | Height (no avatar) | Height (with avatar) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 line | 48dp | 56dp |
| 2 lines | 64dp | 72dp |
| 3 lines | 88dp | 88dp |

Always 16dp horizontal padding.

```kotlin
ListItem(
  headlineContent = { Text("Project Apollo") },
  supportingContent = { Text("Last updated 3 hours ago") },
  leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Folder, null) },
  trailingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.ChevronRight, null) },
  modifier = Modifier.clickable { open() }
)
```

### Dividers

Use `HorizontalDivider()` between sections, not between every item. Material 3
deprecated the always-divided list in favor of section-only dividers.

---

## Motion — Springs Replace Easing

M3 Expressive replaces fixed-duration easing with **spring physics tokens** as the
default for important transitions.

### Spring tokens

```kotlin
// In Compose, the default for state animations
spring<Float>(
  dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy,
  stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMedium
)

// Categories
Spring.DampingRatioHighBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy

Spring.StiffnessHigh
Spring.StiffnessMedium
Spring.StiffnessMediumLow
Spring.StiffnessLow
Spring.StiffnessVeryLow
```

### Easing curves (still available for non-spring)

```kotlin
MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier              // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier            // important transitions
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // incoming elements
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // outgoing
```

### Duration tokens

```
short1 = 50ms
short2 = 100ms
short3 = 150ms
short4 = 200ms
medium1 = 250ms
medium2 = 300ms
medium3 = 350ms
medium4 = 400ms
long1 = 450ms
long2 = 500ms
long3 = 550ms
long4 = 600ms
extraLong1 = 700ms
extraLong2 = 800ms
extraLong3 = 900ms
extraLong4 = 1000ms
```

Default for UI feedback: `short3` (150ms) to `medium1` (250ms).

### When to use spring vs easing

- **Spring**: drag, gesture release, shape morphing, important state changes.
- **Easing**: enter/exit, predictable transitions, simple property changes.

---

## Shape System

M3 has a shape system with five named tokens:

```
extraSmall = 4dp
small = 8dp
medium = 12dp
large = 16dp
extraLarge = 28dp
full = 9999dp (pill)
```

Applied per-component default:
- Buttons → full (pill)
- Cards → medium (12dp)
- Modals / sheets → extraLarge (28dp)
- Inputs → extraSmall (4dp)
- Snackbars → extraSmall

In Compose:
```kotlin
Card(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium) { ... }
```

---

## Snackbars (the Toast equivalent)

```kotlin
val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()

Scaffold(
  snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
) { padding ->
  Button(onClick = {
    scope.launch {
      snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
        message = "Project saved",
        actionLabel = "Undo",
        duration = SnackbarDuration.Short
      )
    }
  }) { Text("Save") }
}
```

- Position: bottom of screen.
- Duration: Short (~4s) / Long (~7s) / Indefinite.
- One snackbar at a time.
- Includes action when reversible.

---

## Material You Dynamic Color

Android 12+ supports user-wallpaper-derived themes. Opt in:

```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  darkTheme -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

For apps where brand identity is critical, **don't** use dynamic color — provide a
fixed `ColorScheme`. For consumer apps where personalization is welcome (Calendar,
Notes, Messages), opt in.

---

## The 15 Android Mobile Rules

**1.** **48dp minimum tap targets.** Material guideline, hard floor.

**2.** **Use Material Components**, don't reinvent buttons, sliders, switches.

**3.** **Roboto Flex** as the default typeface; weight contrast > size contrast.

**4.** **Pill-shaped buttons** as default (M3 Expressive).

**5.** **Bottom navigation 64dp**, max 5 items, labels always visible.

**6.** **Large flexible top app bars** for top-level destinations; small for drill-down.

**7.** **Modal bottom sheets** for actions/filters, not centered dialogs.

**8.** **Spring physics** for state-meaningful motion, not fixed easing.

**9.** **Shape morphing on button press** (M3 Expressive default).

**10.** **Dynamic color** for consumer apps; fixed scheme for brand-critical apps.

**11.** **FAB Menu** for multi-action primary; FAB for single primary.

**12.** **Floating Toolbars** for contextual action sets (deprecated Bottom App Bar).

**13.** **Material 3 list item heights** strict: 48 / 56 / 64 / 72 / 88dp.

**14.** **TalkBack labels** on every Icon-only button (`contentDescription`).

**15.** **Test with TalkBack on**, large font size (200%), and dark theme.

---

## Flutter Material (cross-platform Android target)

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorSchemeSeed: Color(0xFF5E6AD2),
    typography: Typography.material2021(),
  ),
  home: Scaffold(
    appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Home')),
    body: ListView(
      children: [
        ListTile(
          title: Text('Item'),
          trailing: Icon(Icons.chevron_right),
        ),
      ],
    ),
    floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
      onPressed: () { },
      child: Icon(Icons.add),
    ),
    bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
      destinations: [
        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.home), label: 'Home'),
        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.search), label: 'Search'),
      ],
      selectedIndex: 0,
      onDestinationSelected: (i) { },
    ),
  ),
)
```

Flutter's M3 support as of 2026 includes most M3 Expressive components, with FAB
Menu and Floating Toolbar landing in 2025–2026 updates.

---

## Apple vs Material — The Contradictions Table

Cross-platform apps must respect platform conventions. Here's where the systems
diverge:

| Concern | iOS | Material 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Primary action position | Trailing (right) in nav | Bottom right (FAB) or right in app bar |
| Modal style | Bottom sheet with detents | Modal bottom sheet OR dialog |
| Back navigation | Top-left chevron + label | Top-left arrow icon |
| Top nav title | Large title that collapses | Small or Large Flexible app bar |
| Tap target | 44pt | 48dp |
| Font | SF Pro variable | Roboto Flex variable |
| Hierarchy driver | Size + weight (Dynamic Type) | Weight > size (Bold over Big) |
| Button shape default | Capsule (`.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`) | Pill |
| Motion default | Smooth ease | Spring physics |
| Tab bar height | ~49pt (now glass, minimize on scroll) | 64dp (down from 80dp) |
| Empty space treatment | Generous | Slightly tighter |
| Color generation | Custom or system blue | Material You from wallpaper |

For cross-platform: provide a platform-aware shim layer. Don't ship Material UI to
iOS or Cupertino UI to Android.

---

## Hard Bans for Android Pack

- ❌ iOS-style centered dialogs on Android (use bottom sheets).
- ❌ Tap targets below 48dp.
- ❌ Hardcoded colors that ignore Material You / dynamic theming.
- ❌ Bottom app bars (deprecated in M3 Expressive; use Docked/Floating Toolbar).
- ❌ Old M3 navigation bar heights (80dp) — use 64dp.
- ❌ Bold selected labels in nav bar (M3 Expressive changed this default).
- ❌ Fixed-duration easing for state-meaningful transitions (use springs).
- ❌ Pre-Roboto-Flex fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans) when Roboto Flex is available.
- ❌ Ignoring Dynamic Type / font scale settings.
- ❌ Snackbars stacking (one at a time, latest wins).
- ❌ FABs that don't expand to FAB Menu when multiple actions exist.
- ❌ Custom toggles / sliders when Material variants suffice.

3	The semantic system that every component reads from. All tokens are CSS variables

8	
9	## Color System
10	
11	Grain uses **OKLCH** (Oklab Cylindrical) color space. Two reasons:
12	1. Perceptually uniform: equal lightness steps look equally bright across hues.
13	2. Wide gamut: covers P3 displays accurately, falls back to sRGB cleanly.
14	3. Tailwind v4's native color space — no conversion needed.
15	
16	### The Token Hierarchy
17	
18	```
19	Raw tokens (private) → Semantic tokens (public) → Component tokens (specialized)
20	```
21	
22	Components never read raw tokens. Components read semantic. The system has 3 layers
23	so industry packs can override the middle layer without touching components.
24	
25	### Semantic tokens (always present)
26	
27	```css
28	/* Surface and content */
29	--color-bg            /* page background, the lowest layer */
30	--color-surface       /* card / panel background, slightly above bg */
31	--color-surface-2     /* elevated surface, hover backgrounds */
32	--color-fg            /* primary text, icons */
33	--color-muted         /* secondary text */
34	--color-subtle        /* tertiary text, placeholders, disabled */
35	--color-border        /* default border, divider */
36	--color-border-strong /* emphasized border */
37	--color-ring          /* focus ring color */
38	
39	/* Accent (the ONE brand color) */
40	--color-accent        /* primary brand action */
41	--color-accent-fg     /* text/icon on top of accent */
42	--color-accent-soft   /* subtle backgrounds, like badges */
43	--color-accent-strong /* hover/active state of accent */
44	
45	/* Status (semantic, never branded) */
46	--color-success       /* positive state */
47	--color-success-fg
48	--color-success-soft

124	
125	Each industry pack overrides only `--color-accent` and related tokens. Examples:
126	
127	```css
128	/* SaaS (Linear-style) */
129	:root[data-pack="saas"] { --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.14 270); }
130	
131	/* Engineering (Vercel-style — black/white, no accent) */
132	:root[data-pack="engineering"] {
133	  --color-accent: oklch(20% 0.04 265);     /* near-black as accent */
134	  --color-accent-fg: oklch(99% 0.005 270);
135	}
136	
137	/* Corporate (Anthropic-style warm terracotta) */
138	:root[data-pack="corporate"] { --color-accent: oklch(65% 0.14 40); }
139	
140	/* Mobile iOS (system blue) */
141	:root[data-pack="ios"] { --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.18 250); }
142	
143	/* Mobile Android M3 — picks up from dynamic color */
144	:root[data-pack="android"] { --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.16 280); }

146	
147	### Color rules (read alongside Refactoring UI)
148	
149	1. **Limit hues**: 1 brand accent + 4 semantic statuses. Total: 5 distinct hues.
150	2. **Hierarchy by lightness, not hue**: `--color-fg → --color-muted → --color-subtle`
151	   walks down the lightness axis (20% → 55% → 75%) while keeping chroma low and hue
152	   stable. This is the secret to interfaces that read clearly.
153	3. **Saturation conveys interactivity**: high-chroma colors (`--color-accent`) belong
154	   on interactive elements. Neutrals (chroma <0.02) belong on content.
155	4. **Status colors are off-limits for branding**: green is success, red is error,
156	   yellow is warning, blue is info. Never use these for accent decoration.
157	5. **Pure black is banned**: `oklch(20% 0.04 265)` is the default near-black. Pure
158	   `#000` only on display headlines when intentional contrast is the goal.
159	6. **Accent on >25% of surface area is a violation**: the accent is the rarest color.
160	   If the page is half-purple, you've over-applied it.
161	
162	### Contrast requirements
163	
164	WCAG 2.2 AA enforced:
165	- Body text on background: ≥4.5:1
166	- Large text (≥18px or 14px bold): ≥3:1
167	- UI components and graphical objects: ≥3:1 (1.4.11)
168	- Focus indicators: ≥3:1 against adjacent colors (2.4.13)
169	
170	Use `oklch()` lightness math to verify. Anything labeled `--color-fg` or `--color-muted`
171	must clear 4.5:1 against `--color-bg`. `--color-subtle` is for non-essential text only
172	and may sit at 3:1.

175	
176	For charts and graphs, the brand accent is NOT used. Use one of:
177

182	```

206	
207	## Spacing System
208	
209	Base unit: **4px**. Tailwind v4 generates the scale automatically. Use only:
210	
211	| Token | px | When to use |
212	|---|---|---|
213	| `0` | 0 | Reset only |
214	| `0.5` | 2 | Hairline gaps, icon-text alignment |
215	| `1` | 4 | Tight padding inside small badges |
216	| `1.5` | 6 | Compact form padding |
217	| `2` | 8 | Default small padding |
218	| `3` | 12 | Default gap between adjacent items |
219	| `4` | 16 | Default card/component padding |
220	| `5` | 20 | Loose card padding |
221	| `6` | 24 | Section padding (small) |
222	| `8` | 32 | Section padding (medium) |
223	| `10` | 40 | Section padding (large) |
224	| `12` | 48 | Hero padding |
225	| `16` | 64 | Vertical section break |
226	| `20` | 80 | Major section break (marketing) |
227	| `24` | 96 | Marketing hero vertical padding |
228	| `32` | 128 | Reserved — only for spacious editorial layouts |
229	
230	### Spacing rules
231	
232	- **No magic numbers**: every dimension comes from the scale.
233	- **Adjacent elements use small gaps** (2–4 = 8–16px). Sectional separation uses
234	  large gaps (12–24 = 48–96px).
235	- **Internal padding > external margin**: prefer padding inside containers over
236	  margins between them for predictable layouts.
237	- **Container queries for responsive padding**: card padding shrinks at narrow widths
238	  via container queries, not media queries.
239	
240	```css
241	@container (max-width: 480px) {
242	  .card { padding: var(--spacing-3); }
243	}
244	@container (min-width: 481px) {
245	  .card { padding: var(--spacing-5); }
246	}
247	```
248	
249	---
250	
251	## Radius System
252	
253	```css
254	@theme {
255	  --radius-none: 0;
256	  --radius-sm: 0.25rem;    /* 4px - inputs in engineering pack */
257	  --radius-md: 0.375rem;   /* 6px - inputs default */
258	  --radius-lg: 0.5rem;     /* 8px - cards default */
259	  --radius-xl: 0.75rem;    /* 12px - modals, large cards */
260	  --radius-2xl: 1rem;      /* 16px - reserved, marketing only */
261	  --radius-pill: 9999px;   /* capsule - buttons, badges */
262	}
263	```
264	
265	### Radius rules per industry pack
266	
267	| Element | SaaS | Corporate | Engineering | iOS | Android |
268	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
269	| Button | pill | pill | sm (4px) | concentric | pill |
270	| Input | md (6px) | md | sm (4px) | concentric | sm (4dp) |
271	| Card | lg (8px) | xl (12px) | sm (4px) | concentric | xl (12dp) |
272	| Modal | xl (12px) | xl | md (6px) | concentric | 28dp |
273	| Badge | pill | pill | sm | pill | pill |
274	
275	**Concentric (iOS Liquid Glass)**:
276	- Parent radius = R, child radius = R - padding
277	- A button (pill, height 44pt, radius = 22pt) inside a card (radius 12pt, padding 8pt)
278	  is fine as is — but a *child container* of that card with 8pt padding should have
279	  radius = 12 - 8 = 4pt.
280	- Apple's WWDC25 #356 covers this; the API is `.glassEffect()` and `.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`.
281	
282	### Never
283	
284	- Mix radii on touching surfaces. If a button sits inside a card, button's radius
285	  should respect the card's geometry.
286	- Apply `rounded-2xl` to every surface (anti-slop rule #4).
287	- Use `rounded-full` on rectangles wider than 2.5× their height (it looks like a
288	  pill-shaped lozenge, which is correct for narrow elements like badges but ugly
289	  on wider rectangles).
290	
291	---
292	
293	## Motion System
294	
295	```css
296	@theme {
297	  /* Durations */
298	  --duration-instant: 0ms;       /* keyboard actions, frequently-used */
299	  --duration-fast: 100ms;        /* hover, color, opacity */
300	  --duration-normal: 200ms;      /* enter/exit, transforms */
301	  --duration-slow: 300ms;        /* modal, sheet, marketing */
302	  --duration-marketing: 400ms;   /* hero reveals, scroll-driven */
303	
304	  /* Easing curves */
305	  --ease-linear: linear;
306	  --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);       /* default for enter */
307	  --ease-in: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);           /* exit only */
308	  --ease-fluid: cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);        /* Tailwind v4 default */
309	  --ease-snappy: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);       /* fast UI feedback */
310	  --ease-emphasized: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);   /* Material 3 emphasized */
311	  --ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); /* playful bounce */
312	}
313	```
314	
315	### When to use each duration
316	
317	- **instant (0)**: keyboard shortcuts, command palette open, Cmd+K, Esc, frequently-
318	  triggered menus. Anything the user hits >50× per session.
319	- **fast (100ms)**: hover color/opacity changes, focus ring, button press.
320	- **normal (200ms)**: modal/sheet enter, dropdown open, optimistic state confirmation,
321	  list reorder.
322	- **slow (300ms)**: marketing micro-interactions, scroll-triggered fade-in.
323	- **marketing (400ms)**: hero product reveals, parallax, scroll-driven type animation.
324	
325	### Easing rules
326	
327	- Enter animations use `--ease-out` (decelerate into final state).

Clean. Here's what was done and why:

---

## What changed in `theme.dart`

### Color system — 3-layer architecture
Introduced a private `_Palette` raw color layer (components never read this directly). `ThemeColors` now sits in the middle as the semantic layer, using descriptive role names that match M3: `surface`, `surfaceContainer`, `surfaceContainerHigh`, `outline`, `secondary`, `secondaryContainer`. All 30 M3 ColorScheme roles populated explicitly — no gaps that let Flutter auto-derive unexpected tones.

**Fixed brand color** intentionally — Material You dynamic color is off because red/green/amber status semantics (active/clear/police alert) would collide with wallpaper-derived hues.

### Shape system — M3 Expressive
Renamed to M3's own names: `extraSmall=4`, `small=8`, `medium=12`, `large=16`, `extraLarge=28`, `full`. The old `brXs/brSm/brMd/brLg/brXl/br2xl` aliases stay pointing at their original pixel values so no existing widget breaks.

### Motion — M3 duration scale
Added `instant/fast/normal/medium/slow` readable names plus the full M3 granular set (`short1–4`, `medium1–4`, `long1–2`). The `smooth` curve was corrected to M3 Standard easing `Cubic(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` — previously it was `0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0` (which is M2's standard, not M3's emphasized). Added `easeOut/easeIn/emphasized/snappy` curves. Legacy `durFast/durBase/durSlow/durSlower` stay.

### Text — full 15-token M3 scale
Added `displaySmall`, `headlineLarge/Medium/Small`, `titleLarge/Medium/Small`, `bodyLarge/Medium/Small`, `labelLarge/Medium/Small`. All legacy names (`title1`, `body`, `callout`, etc.) aliased to the closest M3 equivalent.

### Component themes — filled in gaps
Added `filledButtonTheme`, `outlinedButtonTheme`, `appBarTheme`, `chipTheme`, `snackBarTheme`, `bottomSheetTheme`, `pageTransitionsTheme`. NavigationBar confirmed at 64dp. Buttons are pill-shaped (`StadiumBorder`), 48dp minimum height per M3 Expressive L-size spec.
